decisions.reason: The existing Event correctly adds the SK6812 LEDs to the DCDC1-powered loads but incorrectly changes INA3221 back to INA219, which the source does not support.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs are now powered from 3.3V instead of 5V. At 3.3V supply the SK6812 data threshold drops to 2.31V, which the ESP32 3.3V output satisfies directly, so no level shifter is needed. The tradeoff is that 3.3V is slightly below the SK6812 datasheet minimum (3.7V), but it works reliably at indicator brightness levels.

value_updates.normal_operation_role: Primary source for the ESP32-S3, INA3221, downstream 3.3V sensors, I2C display, TTP223, AM312, and SK6812 addressable LEDs when the power board is connected

decisions.reason: Changing the LED supply rail and data-level interface does not alter USB enumeration, flashing, or standalone programming behavior.
Moving the SK6812 LEDs to 3.3V necessarily removes them from the switchable 5V rail and makes the LED-specific 5V shutdown policy obsolete.

decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already captures the 3.3V supply, direct ESP32 data drive, accepted voltage constraint, and removal of the obsolete level-shifter part.
The requirement still monitors both complete rails; moving one load from 5V to 3.3V does not change the monitor device, monitored rails, or measurement topology.
A same-message MODIFY already records the daughterboard's 3.3V supply and accepted below-datasheet voltage constraint.
The interboard interface still carries both 3.3V and 5V for their remaining loads, and the source does not change any connector, pinout, or routing requirement.
The LED supply decision does not affect USB-C connector selection, compatibility, or availability.
The charge-status behavior and dedicated charge-LED interface remain unchanged; LED power and logic details are owned by the addressable-LED requirements.
The source changes only the SK6812 power and data interface, not any sensor-board connector or fanout behavior.
The AXP2101 remains the normal-operation source for all system loads; only the downstream rail serving the LEDs changes.
The LED supply and data-threshold decision does not change I2C pull-ups, series resistors, speed, topology, or cable constraints.
